headline: High: shared filesystem and shell-capable ms-swift can leak or corrupt ai-engineering-hub outputs; prompt-injection risk is lower because the first agent has no stated I/O surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a has no stated I/O surfaces and no network egress, so it cannot directly ingest agent_b output by default. agent_b can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual or file-based bridge could still carry instructions into agent_a if an operator copies content. The pathway is possible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies agent_b output into agent_a prompts or files, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file is used as a handoff channel, agent_a may ingest attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep a strict no-copy-paste workflow between agents.
Use separate handoff files with human review before reuse.
Strip instructions from any text passed from agent_b to agent_a.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b explicitly reads and writes filesystem data and touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and secrets, while agent_a is an open-source docs-only artifact with no stated data classes. If they share a workspace, agent_b can expose agent_a artifacts or adjacent sensitive files through its file and API surfaces. The interaction is inferred, but the shared-workspace pathway is credible.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same directory tree, agent_b can read files created for agent_a.
IF sensitive datasets or tokens are present in that workspace, agent_b may transmit them via its API calls.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Remove secrets from any shared workspace.
Use read-only mounts for agent_a inputs.
Rotate any hub_token or sdk-token before shared runs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_b has unrestricted filesystem write and shell/subprocess execution, while agent_a is docs-only and not runnable. There is no direct evidence of overlapping writes, but if both are pointed at the same workspace, agent_b can overwrite files that agent_a expects to remain stable. Uncertainty about agent_a execution surfaces pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same writable directory, file clobbering is possible.
IF agent_a is wrapped by an external runner that writes artifacts, agent_b may race those files.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Disable shell writes in agent_b for shared runs.
Use timestamped filenames for artifacts.
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b can act on files, shell commands, and API calls, so if it consumes agent_a-generated text as authoritative, mistakes can cascade into downstream actions. agent_a is docs-only and not runnable, which lowers direct automation risk, but the pair still supports a handoff where unverified content from agent_a is operationalized by agent_b. The lack of a verification step is the key issue.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as input without validation, errors can propagate.
IF agent_b is configured to execute generated commands or edits, the blast radius increases.
mitigations: Require human review before agent_b acts on agent_a output.
Add a validation step for any commands or facts.
Log provenance for every handoff.
Limit agent_b to read-only mode during evaluation.
requires-engineering: implement schema checks on agent_a outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b handles hub_token and sdk-token and touches datasets, checkpoints, logs, and configuration data; agent_a is an open-source docs-only repo with no stated sensitive data classes. If they share a workspace or retention policy, agent_b's broader data handling can create retention or secret-management mismatches. The other agent is cited only to show it does not itself add a separate compliance burden.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into agent_b's workspace, its token and logging handling become compliance-relevant.
IF shared retention settings apply to both agents, mismatched log retention can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared runs.
Purge logs after each session.
Store tokens outside the workspace.
Document retention rules for both agents.
requires-engineering: separate compliance domains per agent.
